summary:
Sludge volume index is the volume one gram of sludge occupies after thirty minutes of settling, and it is the fastest signal that an activated-sludge plant is about to bulk. It returns sludge volume index, sludge density index, return sludge ratio and return sludge flow, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator returns SVI, the sludge density index and the return-sludge ratio the clarifier needs. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Sludge Volume Index (SVI)
sections.html:
SVI = settled volume (mL/L) × 1 000 ÷ MLSS (mg/L); RAS ratio = MLSS ÷ (RAS MLSS − MLSS)

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
SV₃₀settled sludge volume in 30 minutesmL/L
MLSSmixed liquor suspended solidsmg/L
SVIsludge volume indexmL/g

sections.title: How do I use the Sludge Volume Index (SVI)?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: settled sludge volume after 30 min of 280 mL/L, mlss of 3,000 mg/L, influent flow of 500 m³/day, return sludge mlss of 8,000 mg/L.

Substituting them into the formula gives sludge volume index of 93.33 mL/g, sludge density index of 1.07, return sludge ratio of 60%, return sludge flow of 300 m³/day.

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
The number on its own is not a judgement. These are the bands most often used when the result is quoted in a paper, a report or a label:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
below 80Dense, well settlingexcellent sludge; check for pin floc
80 – 150Normaltypical healthy activated sludge
150 – 250Poor settlinginvestigate loading, aeration and nutrients
above 250Bulkingfilamentous outbreak; the clarifier will lose solids

  • SVI is a ratio, so it rises both when sludge settles badly and when the MLSS reading is too low — always check the MLSS measurement before blaming filaments.

  • Sludge density index is simply 100 ÷ SVI, a measure of how many grams one litre of settled sludge contains.

  • The return-sludge ratio follows from a mass balance on the clarifier: solids leaving in the return must equal solids arriving from the aeration tank.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Reading the settled volume from a stirred or disturbed cylinder.
  • Measuring MLSS from a sample taken at the wrong point in the tank.
  • Raising the return rate to fight bulking without checking whether the clarifier can take the hydraulic load.

faq.q: What does the Sludge Volume Index (SVI) actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns sludge volume index, sludge density index, return sludge ratio and return sludge flow. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
